context.content: Well, I don't have much experience with Sony lenses, or lenses for that mount, so I can't give you my own opinion on them as such. But do you want to buy new only, or is used an option? Because (obviously) you'll get more for your money when buying used. But if you're planning to spend between 500 and 1000€, in the DSLR market it could get you a new D7100 + 18-105 or 18-140mm - or MAYBE even a Canon 80D used with a kit lens, depending on used prices in your area. Both are fantastic DSLR choices in the enthusiast level. Alternatively, for less money, you could get a D5300/D5500 or a D3300/D3400 (you can check Nikon's site for new prices) - you can also read more about all of these models on www.dpreview.com (search at the top). But again you gotta think about whether you think you'll need a DSLR over a Mirrorless, or not. There are benefits to both, for example. **Mirrorless advantages:** Weight; it's much easier to carry around a Mirrorless, the lenses are usually smaller as well. Size; again much easier to carry around, sometimes even in a pocket depending on lenses. Less intruding than a bigger DSLR. **DSLR advantages:** Usually better image quality due to bigger sensors - depending on the camera of course. Bigger selection of lenses and general accessories. Better for moving subjects, sports, animals, kids, etc. ---- But based on what you've said so far, a Mirrorless might be the best choice for you - and if you like landscape photography, you should get a wide lens for it, such as the 16-50mm you mentioned. I don't know about it's macro capability, but you can probably read about that somewhere if you google the lens. There's also this great site: https://www.dxomark.com/Reviews/Best-lenses-for-the-Sony-A6000-Primes-and-Zooms/Best-zoom-lenses-on-the-Sony-A6000 - with suggestions on lenses for the E-mount (sony a6000 etc), with prices and test scores. But the 16-50mm does seem like a good starting lens, with a good focal range. (zoom) Then you can always get the 55-200mm later if you feel like photographing wildlife or the likes.
